transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ethan (Redwood CSM); Liam (CTO, Acumen), Jordan (Data Sci), Maya (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
We dug into the latest scorecard uptick in false positives after prompt pruning. Talked through guardrail thresholds and an approach to quickly triage by labeling 50 examples and running rule-based filters. Agreed to run a dedicated 24 hour throughput test on a quantized variant to measure tail latencies and error surface.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick agenda — scorecard, regressions, guardrail playbook, next steps.
[00:18] Liam (Acumen): yeah sounds good, we've got a couple of engineers on standby but today it's just us. Jordan will talk through the failing cases.
[00:28] Jordan (Acumen): yeah yeah, so after the prompt-reduce sweep last week we saw a jump in false positives on our remediation class. p recision dropped from 0.87 to about 0.73, which is...not great. some of that is prompts being too terse, some are model hallucinations.
[00:45] Priya (Redwood): ok can you give a quick example? is it structural or more the content slipping?
[00:53] Jordan: mostly content, e.g., prompts that used to include a context blob now are shorter, the model's making assumptions. also a handful of edge cases where the guardrail rule fired incorrectly cause of tokenization mismatch.
[01:10] Alex: hmm tokenization mismatch — do you mean K V cache alignment or more like special chars?
[01:16] Jordan: uh mostly punctuation and our newline-normalization; sometimes the rule engine is matching on the wrong substring — transcription says substring but it's more like a regex boundary issue.
[01:30] Liam: to be clear, we need the system to keep precision above 0.8 for the remediation classifier, otherwise product won't ship. timeline is tight.
[01:41] Maya: and scope — this pilot is in the U.S. only; we care about latency under 300ms p90 for the hosted endpoint, but if dedicated gives better and costs are within reason we'll look at that too.
[02:00] Priya: quick note — p90 300ms on hosted with our default batching is tight; dedicated with optimized kernels and quantization usually helps but we need to validate tail behavior. we'll propose a dedicated-quant variant for the 24h run.
[02:18] Jordan: what's the expected tradeoff on quality with the quantized model?
[02:23] Priya: in our experience it's minimal for this class of model, but we need to check prompt fidelity; sometimes very terse prompts expose minor hallucination differences after quant. so that's why we want labeled cases.
[02:37] Ethan (Redwood): also note caching — prefix/KV cache hit rate matters. if your calls are mostly repeated contexts we can shave a lot off the p50/p90. please share distribution of unique contexts.
[02:51] Liam: we can share, though ~60% are unique per session.
[02:55] Alex: okay lets talk regression playbook. step one: customer tags 50 failing examples (25 FP, 25 FN) in the shared sheet. step two: SE runs a prompt-sweep / guardrail param scan locally, records candidate fixes and delta on scorecard. step three: if candidate fixes are small, do a canary roll; if not, rollback to previous pinned model and open an ops ticket.
[03:25] Maya: can you define "small"? we need thresholds to decide canary vs rollback automatically.
[03:32] Priya: yeah good call. propose small = delta in precision < 0.03 and no regression in recall, and latency delta p90 < 10%. if any of those exceed, we go rollback.
[03:45] Jordan: sounds fair. can we automate the comparison in the scorecard so it's eyeball free?
[03:51] Alex: yes, I'll update the scorecard template to include auto flags.
[03:56] [00:04:00] Priya: on guardrails — we're seeing a number of false positives that look rule-based. i'd like to carve a short regex/whitelist step that runs pre-model to soak obvious matches. sometimes it's cheaper to add a quick deterministic filter than touch model prompts.
[04:18] Liam: do we risk masking true positives with whitelist?
[04:22] Priya: that's why we want labeled examples first; apply the filter to the 50 examples and measure impact. if it hurts recall we back it out.
[04:33] Jordan: also quick note — some of our logs show 500 errors around 02:00 UTC yesterday, maybe a downstream infra issue. not sure if it's on Redwood side or ours.
[04:45] Ethan: we'll pull the request ids from the 24h run and correlate, priya will include request_id sampling.
[04:52] [00:05:00] Alex: let's cover the dedicated run specifics — Priya, what config you want?
[05:00] Priya: dedicated-quant v2, batch size observed at 8 (we'll test 4/8/16), KV-cache enabled, sequence length cap 1024 for the test, run for 24 hours with synthetic replay of typical traffic. collect p50/p90/p99, error-rate, kv-hit rate, and token throughput.
[05:20] Maya: cost estimate? we need a ballpark to sign off on a dedicated run.
[05:24] Alex: rough ballpark — a single GPU dedicated 24h with quantized model is in the low thousands USD; i'll send an exact line item after this call.
[05:36] Liam: fine. also on security — we need SOC2 attestation and audit logs for any dedicated instance. have we got that?
[05:45] Ethan: Redwood has SOC 2 type II and we can surface audit logs; for private deployments we do KMS integration. we'll attach the security pack.
[05:55] [00:06:00] Jordan: back to scoring — our current scorecard bins by scenario, but we want to add a "prompt-length" dimension and token budget column to see correlation.
[06:10] Priya: easy to add. also recommend adding a field for "pre-filtered by rule" boolean so we can separate rule-hits from model-hits.
[06:20] Alex: agreed. Jordan, you'll add flags in the shared sheet.
[06:26] Jordan: yep I'll do that.
[06:30] Maya: what's the timeline if we find the quant model causes a small drop? could we canary for 6 hours and then fold back?
[06:36] Priya: yes, we have a canary plan: roll to 5% traffic for 6 hours, monitor auto-flags in scorecard (precision/recall), and if everything passes, increase incrementally. rollback immediately if precision delta > 0.03 or latency p90 > 10% beyond baseline.
[06:55] [00:07:00] Liam: do you have automated rollback or is it manual?
[07:00] Alex: can be automated via policy, but typically for enterprise pilots we do manual rollback for visibility; we can enable auto for later.
[07:08] Jordan: curious — any known differences for quant with your runtime? we've seen noisy logits in other runtimes.
[07:16] Priya: our runtime uses kernel selection and specific attention optimizations; we do a calibration step for quant to reduce distribution shift. usually that helps. occasionally you see small differences in edge cases — which is why we labeled examples.
[07:33] [00:08:00] Maya: ok, action items recap?
[07:36] Alex: Priya runs dedicated-quant 24h, shares logs + request ids. Alex sends updated scorecard and pricing. Jordan tags 50 examples. Maya finalizes acceptance criteria and stakeholder list.
[07:50] Ethan: i'll attach the security pack and SOC2 link in the follow-up.
[07:56] [00:09:00] Jordan: one more thing — we noticed a small cluster of hallucinations tied to a specific prompt template used for the remediation messages. would it make sense to test a conservative templating approach?
[08:08] Priya: yes, test a conservative sub-prompt that includes explicit "do not assume" clauses; also try anchor context with a short schema. we can A/B those in the canary.
[08:20] Liam: okay.
[08:22] [00:10:00] Alex: timeline recap: 24h run by 9/27, scorecard template by 9/25, labels by 9/29, deep-dive next week. any blockers?
[08:34] Maya: none from product. just need the pricing line item.
[08:38] Alex: will send.
[08:40] [00:11:00] Priya: quick note about logs — please enable debug sampling for 0.1% of requests so we don't flood the logs but we get full KV and prompt context for failing cases.
[08:52] Jordan: done, will toggle.
[08:55] [00:12:00] Ethan: security question from procurement — can you show support for customer-managed KMS if we move to private?
[09:02] Alex: yes for private deployments we support KMS / HSM integrations; for dedicated we can do customer-managed keys in the region depending on contract.
[09:12] Liam: good.
[09:15] [00:13:00] Maya: any competitor notes we should be aware of? we did a quick trial with CobaltAI, their latency was lower for short prompts but quality variance was higher. also NimbusServe offered integrated SSO which we liked.
[09:30] Alex: noted, we can highlight our SSO and audit capabilities and the calibration step that reduces quality variance.
[09:38] [00:14:00] Jordan: small nit — some product names in your docs got mis-typed in the shared deck; "Redwood Dedicated" is sometimes shown as "Redwood dedicat" in the export, not a big deal but FYI.
[09:48] Priya: thanks, we'll fix that.
[09:51] [00:15:00] Alex: ok final check — anything else?
[09:55] Liam: just make sure the canary playbook is in writing and the auto-rollback thresholds are explicit.
[10:02] Alex: will do. thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[10:08] Maya: thanks everyone.
[10:10] End of call.
